authoredPrompt: This figure is a perspective sketch of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire, combined with a right-hand-rule demonstration. A gray cylindrical wire runs horizontally across the full width of the drawing. At the left, a realistically rendered right hand grips the wire in a closed fist with the thumb extended along it toward the right; just beyond the hand, a short red arrow labeled I points the same way. Along the right half of the wire, four identical sets of concentric blue circles encircle it, each set drawn as nested ellipses so they read as circles centered on the wire in planes perpendicular to it. Within every set the rings crowd together near the wire and stand progressively farther apart outward, and each carries arrowheads marking a common sense of circulation that matches the wrap of the fingers. A bold label B with a vector arrow sits above the rightmost set. Pairing the gripping hand with the ring sets asks the reader to match thumb to current and finger wrap to field direction, while the widening spacing encodes the field weakening with distance.
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle for current direction: the learner switches the red I arrow between rightward and leftward, the hand thumb flips and every blue field-line arrow reverses, making the right-hand-rule link between current direction and magnetic-field circulation explicit.
- Slider for distance from the wire: the learner drags a radial marker outward through the concentric loops, the B readout falls and the highlighted loop moves into wider spacing, showing that the field around a long straight wire weakens with radius.
authoredContext:
The magnetic field lines of the infinite wire are circular and centered at the wire (the figure), and they are identical in every plane perpendicular to the wire. Since the field decreases with distance from the wire, the spacing of the field lines must increase correspondingly with distance. The direction of this magnetic field may be found with a second form of the right-hand rule (illustrated in the figure). If you hold the wire with your right hand so that your thumb points along the current, then your fingers wrap around the wire in the same sense as B→.

Some magnetic field lines of an infinite wire. The direction of B→ can be found with a form of the right-hand rule.

This figure demonstrates the right-hand rule. The wire is held with the right hand so that the thumb points along the current. The fingers wrap around the wire in the same sense as the magnetic field.

The direction of the field lines can be observed experimentally by placing several small compass needles on a circle near the wire, as illustrated in the figure. When there is no current in the wire, the needles align with Earth’s magnetic field. However, when a large current is sent through the wire, the compass needles all point tangent to the circle. Iron filings sprinkled on a horizontal surface also delineate the field lines, as shown in the figure.

discrepancies: The right hand is reduced to a crude skin-colored sphere blob with a few cylinder fingers/thumb and does not read as a hand gripping the wire, unlike the detailed anatomical hand in the source.
The red current arrow (I) is tiny and barely visible near the hand, whereas in the source it is a prominent red arrow between the hand and the field rings.
An extra orange torus marker ring appears around the wire that is not present in the source figure.
The I and B labels are rendered very small and are hard to read compared to the clear bold labels in the source.
evaluation.notes: The core right-hand-rule concept (wire, gripping hand, concentric blue B-field rings with circulation arrows, B label) is present and the reverse-current and distance-slider interactions are meaningful and correct, but the hand is a crude blob, the red current arrow is far too small, and the I/B labels are poorly legible.
action_items: Enlarge the red current arrow and place it clearly between the hand and the rings so it matches the prominent red I arrow in the source.
Rebuild the hand so it visibly reads as a right hand gripping the wire with the thumb pointing along the current direction.
Increase the font size and weight of the I and B labels for legibility and to match the source hierarchy.
Remove or visually de-emphasize the orange torus marker (or clearly tie it to the slider) since it is an element absent from the source figure.
